To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structural and morphological changes of nanocrystals in the presence of a reagent can be observed in real time by in situ transmission electron microscopy.
the structural similarity between the precursor and product phases and the mobility of ions inside the crystal determine the reaction pathway (displacement or conversion).

the structural similarity between the reactant and product phases, as well the mobility of ions in the reactant phase, exert a strong controlling influence on the mechanism and pathway of chemical reactions in individual nanocrystals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of chemical reactions in nanocrystals.
the development of novel nanocrystal-based materials and devices.
the synthesis of nanomaterials and nanocomposites, and the characterization of their properties and structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction mechanism is dependent upon the crystal structure and composition.
the reaction pathway is dictated by the structural similarity between the starting and ending products, as well as by the mobility of the ions in the crystal.
the reaction pathway in nanocrystals depends on their crystal structure and the ability of ions in that structure to move.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reaction pathways for sulfide nanocrystal reactions with lithium are determined by a combination of crystal structure, composition, size, and surface energy.
the reaction pathway is determined by the structure and composition of the initial phase and that this can be used to control the reaction pathway.
the reaction pathway of nanocrystals is strongly influenced by the structural and chemical properties of the nanocrystals, and the reaction pathways are distinct from those in the bulk materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in situ studies of nanocrystal transformations are critical to understanding the mechanisms of chemical reactions in nanoscale systems.
the reaction mechanism is determined by the structure, composition, size, and morphology of the nanocrystals.
nanoscale size effects are important for understanding the reaction mechanisms in nanocrystals.
